title: Science Tonight on Instagram: "The AI reporter finally revealed why they are drinking so much water!
content: This is one side of why I think it's worth it to doodle or describe your dreams in words, rather than depending on ai to recreate a similar image to your dream. Another side of being against ai in dream studies is the extremely impressionable brain that remembers memories. Every time you remember a memory, you warp it through your own human errors. Your memory and information storage in your brian is all just references from experiences, references of data collected from sensory input. Every time we access that data, we are changing it a little bit. So every single time your eyes take in visual data that is ai, you're inputting data to your memory that COMES FROM an amalgamation of data that was sourced from EVERYWHERE, and reshuffled. So imagine you're having these dreams that are building architecture and emotional tones from your real life experiences (data input) and you're amazed that your dreams are eerily similar to so many other's dreams. And you wanna share data of human experiences with each other to compare and contrast, and all the sudden a huge amount of data is actually computer data that mimics the human data collecting experience but now that data is coming from things you yourself have not inputted, and when you go "wow my memory data- that is an amalgamation of my lived experiences- looks so much like this computer data that is copying and recreating human experiences from the entire internet and turning it into an amalgamation! There's something to this, look at this images guys! Input this non-experiencial data into your mushy human brain and let it intermingle with the actual experiencial data, mix it all up and then go back to sleep and hope to have an original dream experience!" It's just kind of like, a snake eating it's tail. We can't use something that is a weird low quality mimic of our own sensory input and information storage/withdrawal, and think it's actually going to help anyone understand the workings of shared and extremely similar reoccurring dream experiences. It's just messing up your data. You look at enough ai pics and you're going to see your own mallworld in it, because it's doing exactly what all our brains are also doing, but way shittier and with really negative consequences to our health.
